title: POC scoping: Orchid Data x Redwood - latency SLOs
summary: Orchid Data is scoping a 6-week POC to validate latency/throughput SLOs for an in-product summarization feature. Primary success criteria: TTFT p95 <= 200ms (p99 <= 400ms) for short prompts, sustained token throughput to support 30 concurrent users with max TPOT ~20ms/token (approx 50 tokens/sec aggregate per user) with overall 99th percentile tail avoidance. Plan: run baseline benchmarks against their current self-hosted Llama variant, then run Redwood hosted and Dedicated profiles (quantized and fp16). Measurement plan includes representative prompt corpus, burst testing (Poisson + spikes), warm/cold-run separation, and 95/99 reporting windows. Next steps include sharing benchmarking harness, scheduling lab run, and providing pricing/ops notes for Dedicated capacity.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-01 14:00 PT | Duration 36 minutes | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), John (Orchid CTO), Maria (Product), Sam (ML Eng)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros - I'm Alex Chen, AE on the Redwood side. Priya is our SE who will own the benchmarking and technical run through.
[00:18] John: Hi, John Park here, CTO at Orchid. Maria and Sam are on. we're trying to scope a POC to validate latency before we commit to embedding the model in our live product.
[00:28] Maria: yes, user experience is very sensitive to first token. if TTFT is bad customers notice.
[00:35] Priya: absolutely, that's why we typically separate TTFT (time-to-first-token) from TPOT - time-per-output-token or steady-state token latency; both matter but trade offs differ for cost and batching.
[00:50] Sam: quick clarification, when you say TPOT is that measured as ms/token or tokens/sec? we measure throughput in tok/s usually.
[00:58] Priya: good call - we report both. TPOT often expressed as ms per token for latency centric SLOs, and tokens/sec for throughput capacity planning. in this call I'll reference ms/token and aggregate tokens/sec when we talk concurrent users.
[01:15] Alex: can you give the current baseline for Orchid? what model, infra, and observed p95/p99 numbers?
[01:23] John: we're running a self-hosted Llama-2 13B quantized on a mix of A100s; our rough numbers from ad-hoc tests are TTFT p95 around 300ms, p99 close to 700ms - which is higher than we'd like. steady-state per-token latency is around 25-30ms/token. that's with some homegrown batching.
[01:45] Sam: also note our prompt lengths are short - median 40 tokens, 95th ~180, but we do have occasional 800 token long contexts for special cases.
[01:58] Priya: thanks, that helps. for a POC we usually define success criteria up front - example: TTFT p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 400ms for typical prompts (<= 200 tokens). and TPOT p95 <= 20ms/token for steady-state, with the ability to sustain 30 concurrent interactive users with 95% of requests meeting those targets. does that align with your UX goals?
[02:24] Maria: yes, p95 <=200ms would be a big improvement. what's realistic for p99 though? users do notice rare tails.
[02:30] Priya: p99 is tougher; we aim p99 <= 400ms for TTFT in most Dedicated configs. hosted (multi-tenant) gives good median but may have higher tails unless you pick a dedicated pool. we can show both profiles in the benchmark.
[02:45] Alex: cost is also a factor - Orchid asked for an estimate of how Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private will trade off for latency.
[02:53] John: yes cost/perf is key. we'd trade some cost for better p99s.
[03:00] Priya: plan wise - we'll run three benchmark phases: 1) baseline against your current infra (you run harness, we help analyze), 2) Redwood hosted tests (same model config, our clusters), 3) Redwood Dedicated with quantization variants (4-bit/8-bit) and kernel optimizations. we'll capture TTFT, per-token latencies, batch sizes, and throughput under stationary and burst traffic.
[03:25] Sam: how do you handle warm vs cold? warm caches (KV cache) change TTFT a lot.
[03:30] Priya: we'll separate cold-start (cold worker, empty KV) and warm (hot KV, cached prefix) runs. cold starts measured after node spin-up and after idle periods. warm runs emulate steady-state traffic. for user-facing features TTFT warm p95 is most representative but cold matters for scale-to-zero or ephemeral workers.
[03:48] Maria: what about TPOT under burst? our product sees spikes during daily digest sends.
[03:55] Priya: we'll run Poisson traffic plus scheduled spikes at 5x baseline to observe queueing and tail behavior. we also run concurrency sweeps - e.g. 5, 10, 20, 30 concurrent interactive users - and measure aggregate tokens/sec and % requests meeting p95 targets.
[04:12] Alex: measurement windows and reporting - do you do rolling 5m windows or single-run percentiles?
[04:18] Priya: both. primary SLO reporting uses 15-minute windows with p95/p99 calculated over the window to smooth out noise; we also provide single-run percentiles (end-to-end) for the benchmark. we'll include raw traces so you can compute other slices by prompt length, model branch, and region.
[04:36] John: security: we'll need SSO, SOC2 docs and an NDA. also data residency - some prompts contain PII.
[04:44] Alex: we will share SOC2 & infra docs; for the POC we can run with anonymized prompts or on a Private/VPC test if needed. we'll include minimal required compliance docs in the pack.
[04:55] Sam: for the harness, we use a mix of synthetic prompts and real user traces. Sam will sanitize and share 1k examples.
[05:02] Maria: timeline? you mentioned 6 weeks earlier.
[05:06] Alex: typical POC: week 0-1 prep and data collection, week 2 baseline run and analysis, week 3 Redwood hosted runs, week 4 Dedicated runs and quantization experiments, week 5 iterate on config and re-run, week 6 results and decision. can compress if you have infra ready and quick callbacks.
[05:26] John: sounds reasonable. our ideal is to finish by end of Sep so we can decide for Q4 rollout.
[05:33] Priya: measurement specifics: standard metrics we'll capture and report as strings in the benchmark CSV: run_id, sample_id, prompt_len, TTFT_ms, token_n, per_token_ms_series (we give aggregated ms/token), total_latency_ms, worker_state (cold|warm), model_variant, batch_size, concurrency_level.
[05:55] Sam: when you run quantized 4-bit, how do you expect quality to degrade? we need quality guards - probably a BLEU or embedding-sim threshold.
[06:03] Priya: we attach quality evals: we will run the prompt set through model variants and compute embedding cosine and a human-verified sample set; we set a quality guard that average embedding similarity must be >= 0.95 to baseline, and spot-checks for hallucination. if quantization causes >5% degradation in quality metrics we'll note it as a blocker.
[06:22] Alex: success criteria recap - functional: output quality within agreed threshold; non-functional: TTFT p95 <= 200ms, TTFT p99 <= 400ms, TPOT p95 <= 20ms/token, sustain 30 concurrent users with >=95% of requests meeting p95. business: pricing within target budget we discussed via mail.
[06:45] Maria: can you include sample dashboards or what the report will look like?
[06:50] Priya: yes, we'll provide per-route dashboards with token-level breakdowns, p95/p99 heatmaps, and trace samples. we will also provide the raw CSV and a summary deck.
[07:02] John: any caveats?
[07:05] Priya: sure - environment differences (networking, storage) can shift TTFT. hosted runs isolate infra variables, Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor effects. also cold-starts depend on autoscaling profile; if you require scale-to-zero that's a different SLO.
[07:20] Sam: do you support KV cache persistence across calls?
[07:23] Priya: yes we support prefix/KV caching; in Dedicated we can pin workers to keep KV warm. we'll test both pinned and ephemeral modes.
[07:33] Alex: ok next practicals - Sam to share prompt set by Tuesday (2027-08-03). Alex will push harness and runbook by Friday (2027-08-05). Priya will book time with your infra to run baseline the week of 8/9.
[07:50] Maria: and we'll expect a pricing sheet and Dedicated sizing options.
[07:55] Alex: yes will include sizing with example throughput maps (tokens/sec per GPU).
[08:02] John: great, thanks. any final Qs?
[08:05] Sam: none here.
[08:06] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifact links and calendar invites.
[08:10] (end)
